official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 order decisions
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Inspectorate publishes decisions and maps for rights-of-way orders separately from start-date, hearing and inquiry notices; a notice is not a confirmed order.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current procedure guidance
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Rights of Way guidance booklet was updated 22 April 2026 and distinguishes definitive map modification orders from public path orders and their objection procedures.

official_measurement_examples.name: Definitive map evidence
official_measurement_examples.fact: A recorded public right of way is a public access right and does not establish ownership of the underlying land.

official_measurement_examples.name: Order versus existing route
official_measurement_examples.fact: A proposed diversion, extinguishment or modification order must not be treated as if the definitive route has already changed before confirmation and effective-date requirements are satisfied.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning permission does not by itself divert or extinguish an existing public right of way; separate legal procedures may be required.

official_measurement_examples.name: Landowner notice
official_measurement_examples.fact: June 2026 Planning Inspectorate checklist guidance requires affected landowners to be identified and served notice or an appropriate Secretary of State direction obtained where ownership cannot be identified.

official_measurement_examples.name: Map precision limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Online or local rights-of-way mapping should retain source and legal status and must not be treated as cadastral title geometry or surveyed development setback.

official_measurement_examples.name: Promotion guard
official_measurement_examples.fact: No parcel access clearance or Future Growth score is promoted while recovery is parked.

core_rules: public right of way is not land ownership
order notice is not confirmed order
proposed route change is not current definitive route
planning permission does not divert or extinguish PROW
definitive map modification and public path orders remain distinct
landowner notification process is separate from route ownership
map geometry is not cadastral title
PROW evidence does not determine development yield
historical and current orders retain status and dates
no promotion while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Planning Inspectorate, GOV.UK and legislation sources checked on 2026-07-26. April-July 2026 rights-of-way procedure and notices were retained with definitive-map/order/ownership/planning separation; no parcel promotion.
